rows: Polygons are split by local authority; boundary polygons can occur in both files and use Land Registry-INSPIRE IDs.
Indicative extents are not legal title plans.
Current publication is dated 5 July 2026 and is replaced on the first Sunday monthly; Enfield, Havering and Lambeth are listed.
Catalogue presence does not prove downloaded ZIP bytes.
HMLR captures the data against British National Grid and supplies open GML.
Conversion or reprojection requires explicit provenance.
Official bare-earth 1m composite is available through WCS and uses national LiDAR sources.
Metadata does not prove current row-specific response bytes.
EA documents a persistent WCS 2.0.1 endpoint for DTM1m raw-pixel access.
Requested and final endpoint identity still require response receipts.
Official 2m DTM is referenced to Newlyn and supports resolution sensitivity.
It cannot replace the pinned 1m primary metric.
Survey resources provide temporal and source context for LiDAR coverage.
Composite-pixel lineage must still be bound per result.
Terrain 50 is updated annually in July and supplied as 10km tiles with regular 50m posts.
It is a coarse secondary check.
ASCII grid and GML are supplied together; tile grid spacing and vertical reference metadata are defined.
Per-tile metadata identifies product and tile lineage under GEMINI/INSPIRE conventions.
Metadata must be paired and hashed with the exact tile.
Grid and contour products are supplied as compressed geographic tiles.
Multiple editions of one tile must not be co-sampled.
The product documents grid/contour structures and pixel-centre semantics.
Documentation does not validate a downloaded archive.
WCS separates discovery, coverage description and retrieval while binding domain and range.
Clients must verify service, selected coverage, axes, domain and range.
WCS can expose explicit interpolation controls.
Timeout and process cleanup are explicit subprocess responsibilities; bounded communication and termination are documented.
A parent timeout alone does not prove descendant-process cleanup.
Path.replace provides replacement semantics and resolved paths support containment checks.
Atomicity still depends on same-filesystem use and correct temporary-file handling.
